items.title: Jürgen Schmidhuber joins Sakana AI as Chief Scientific Advisor
items.summary_en: Sakana AI announced that AI researcher Jürgen Schmidhuber has joined the company as Chief Scientific Advisor, a role in which he will guide the direction of Sakana AI's Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) Lab while keeping his existing positions and traveling regularly to Tokyo. Sakana AI's post frames his 1980s work on recursive self-improvement and meta-learning as foundational to some of the company's recent research, including the Darwin Gödel Machine and The AI Scientist.

items.title: Sakana AI launches Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2 multi-agent orchestration systems
items.summary_en: Sakana AI released two new versions of its Fugu orchestration system: Fugu Max, aimed at cost-efficiency by routing tasks across a pool of open-weight and specialized models, and Fugu Ultra v2, aimed at higher-quality output for complex reasoning, research and software-engineering tasks using a deeper model pool. Per the announcement, Fugu is not a foundation model itself but a trained router/orchestrator that can also recursively call instances of itself; both tiers are available through Sakana's OpenAI-compatible API.

items.title: Sakana AI researchers publish PC-ALM, a backpropagation-free training method for very deep networks
items.summary_en: Sakana AI researchers Jeffrey Seely and Julian Gould published work on Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding (PC-ALM), a layer-local alternative to backpropagation. According to the publication, PC-ALM trains residual networks up to 1,000 layers deep using only local layer-to-layer updates, reaching accuracy within about two percentage points of standard backpropagation on benchmark image classification tasks, and the team released an MIT-licensed JAX reference implementation.

items.title: Sakana AI forms business partnership with Sumitomo Corporation and SCSK
items.summary_en: Sakana AI, SCSK Corp, and Sumitomo Corporation announced a comprehensive business partnership to accelerate deployment of domestically developed AI across Japanese industry, with initial focus on finance and manufacturing and consideration of cybersecurity and overseas expansion. The arrangement combines Sakana AI's model and product development with SCSK's systems-integration expertise and Sumitomo Corporation's business network, which the announcement describes as reaching roughly 100,000 companies.
